report.tagline: India's biggest job site, free for job seekers and paid by recruiters who want to find and reach candidates.
report.simpleSummary: Naukri is where most Indian office workers keep their CV. Job seekers upload a profile for free and apply to jobs. Companies and recruitment agencies pay Naukri to post jobs and to search its giant CV database. Because almost everyone is already there, recruiters keep paying and Naukri makes very high profits.

overview.whatItDoes: Naukri is an online jobs board run by Info Edge since 1997. Job seekers create profiles, search jobs and apply for free. Recruiters pay to post jobs, search CVs (a tool called Resdex) and use AI tools to screen and contact candidates. It also sells paid boosts and AI tools to job seekers.
howItWorks: Job seekers make a free profile with CV, skills, salary and notice period.
Recruiters buy job posting packs and Resdex access to search CVs by skills, city and experience.
Naukri matches jobs and candidates and sends alerts by app, email and WhatsApp.
AI-Rex helps recruiters search, screen, message and shortlist candidates.
Job seekers can pay for Naukri FastForward style boosts, AI Resume Maker and AI Mock Interview tools.
Premium brands like iimjobs, hirist and PremiumX serve senior and tech hiring.
overview.valueProposition: For recruiters: the largest pool of Indian white-collar candidates in one place, so they can fill roles fast. For job seekers: free access to most openings and a chance to be found by recruiters without applying.

businessModel.summary: Naukri is freemium: job seekers use it free, and recruiters pay. Most money comes from companies and agencies buying subscriptions for job posts and CV database search. A small share comes from job seekers buying boosts and AI tools.

revenueStreams.detail: Resdex CV search and job posting packs sold to companies and agencies. The biggest stream.
AI-Rex, PremiumX, Talent Pulse and employer branding sold to large firms.
Profile boosts, resume writing, AI tools.
iimjobs, hirist and Naukri Top Tier for senior and tech roles.

businessModel.pricing: Single job posts cost roughly ₹400 to ₹1,650 depending on type (standard, classified, hot vacancy). Resdex starts at a few thousand rupees for small packs. Large firms sign custom annual deals. Prices change often, so these are approximate.
costDrivers: Staff, especially a large sales team that sells to SMEs and agencies
Advertising to job seekers (Info Edge spent ₹118 crore on ads in Q4 FY26 across brands)
Tech and AI build-out (₹150 crore planned in FY27)
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take one small recruiter paying around ₹50,000 a year. Naukri's cost to serve them is mostly sales effort and servers, because the candidates are already there and job seekers bring themselves. So a large part of that ₹50,000 becomes profit. Naukri's recruitment arm has long run at an operating margin of over 50%, meaning more than ₹50 of every ₹100 is left after costs. This margin figure is from past Info Edge results, so treat it as an estimate for FY26.

howTheyGetUsers: Google searches for jobs, where Naukri ranks high
Brand built over 25+ years with TV ads
Recruiters are found by Naukri's sales team city by city
whatBringsUsersBack: Job switches every 2 to 3 years in IT and services
Recruiters renew because hires come from the database
growth.moat: A two-sided network: recruiters pay because the candidates are there, and candidates stay because recruiters are there. With 11.8 crore profiles and 25 years of data, a new job site cannot match its database or search quality quickly. Strong profits also let Naukri spend more on AI than rivals.

competitors.name: LinkedIn
competitors.positioning: Professional network with jobs, used heavily for senior and global roles.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Naukri has more mid-level and mass hiring in India and a cheaper, search-first database, while LinkedIn wins on networking and passive senior talent.

competitors.name: Indeed
competitors.positioning: Global job search engine with free and paid posts.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Naukri has deeper Indian CV data and a strong recruiter sales team.

competitors.name: Apna and WorkIndia
competitors.positioning: Apps for blue-collar and entry-level jobs in local languages.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Naukri focuses on white-collar jobs and is weaker for delivery, retail and factory roles.

competitors.name: foundit (formerly Monster India)
competitors.positioning: Older job board with a similar model.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Naukri has much bigger traffic and profiles.

improvementIdeas.idea: Verified recruiter badge plus one-tap 'report scam' with fast action
improvementIdeas.problem: Fake jobs and scam calls break trust
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer scams and more job seekers replying to real recruiters
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Scam reports per 1,000 active users and reply rate

improvementIdeas.idea: Monthly 'still looking?' nudge that freezes profiles not updated in 6 months
improvementIdeas.problem: Recruiters waste credits on outdated CVs
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher recruiter reply rates and renewals
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of contacted profiles that reply

improvementIdeas.idea: Application status updates: recruiters must mark viewed or rejected, with AI-Rex doing it automatically
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Better job seeker experience and more return visits
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of applications with a status update within 14 days

improvementIdeas.idea: Pay-per-hire pricing pilot for small businesses
improvementIdeas.problem: SMEs drop off due to upfront subscription cost
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More SME customers and lower churn

pmLessons: Make one side free and charge the side that gets the most value. For Naukri, recruiters pay because they need candidates more urgently.
Data built over years can be a stronger moat than features.
A strong sales team matters in B2B, even for an online product.
Add AI to the part of the job users hate most, like screening CVs, so they will pay for it.
Trust problems like scams can hurt the free side and slowly weaken the paid side.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce fake job scams on Naukri?
interviewQuestions.hint: Define the scam types, find where they start (fake recruiter accounts, off-platform calls), suggest verification, reporting and warnings, and measure scam reports and trust.

interviewQuestions.question: LinkedIn is growing in India. How should Naukri respond?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare user segments. Defend mid-level and mass hiring, use AI to improve match quality, and avoid copying social features blindly.

interviewQuestions.question: What metric would you use to judge AI-Rex?
interviewQuestions.hint: Time saved per hire, shortlist to interview rate, paid conversion, and renewal of AI-Rex customers.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Naukri charge job seekers more?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh extra revenue against hurting the free supply side. Suggest only tools that help candidates win, not paid visibility that annoys recruiters.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you enter blue-collar hiring?
interviewQuestions.hint: Different users need vernacular, voice and WhatsApp flows. Consider a separate brand, partner with staffing firms and price per hire.
